# Implementation Plan — Description

**North Star:** Re-architect Gandalf onto the Crucible/Foreman pipeline using a vertically sliced, event-sourced 'Broad-First' planning engine, pulling the Ledger Reducer and Hypothesis Generation forward to rigorously test Merge Gate timeouts, schema validation, and structural orthogonality.

Implement 'Broad-First' planning (matrix-based) and parallelized exploration for Gandalf. Overhaul to use the new Crucible/Foreman pipeline. CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS: 1) Force a vertically sliced architecture. 2) Pull the Ledger Reducer into Phase 1 to prove event sourcing works. 3) Pull primitive hypothesis generation into Phase 2 so the Merge Gate can be actually tested. 4) Demand concrete mechanisms for structural orthogonality (no prompt injection), strict timeouts at the Merge Gate, and schema-validated event ingestion.

## Success criteria
- Architecture is vertically sliced, avoiding monolithic phase blocks.
- Ledger Reducer is fully implemented and active in Phase 1, proving the event-sourcing contract.
- Primitive hypothesis generation is active in Phase 2, feeding directly into a testable Merge Gate.
- Merge Gate enforces strict, configuration-driven timeouts to prevent infinite stalls.
- All ingested events are validated against a strict JSON schema before entering the Ledger.
- Structural orthogonality is proven via isolated execution contexts, preventing prompt injection across sub-agents.

## Provenance

Generated by Crucible Stage 2 from an approved Master Plan, vetted by the Shark-Tank loop and the well-formedness gate before handoff.
